report:
Brain, left thalamic tumour

Received in formalin are fragments of soft tumour tissue from the thalamus, measuring 45 x 35 x 20 mm in aggregate. The cut surface is soft and grey-tan with areas of haemorrhage and yellow necrosis. Representative sections are taken; see block key.

(A1-A6) tumour.

Specimen
- Procedure: Craniotomy and debulking
- Tumour site: Left thalamus
- Extent of resection as stated by the surgeon: Partial resection / debulking
- Specimen integrity: Fragmented, received in pieces

Microscopic findings
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show a diffusely infiltrating glial neoplasm composed of small to
  medium-sized cells with hyperchromatic angulated nuclei. The tumour shows
  increased cellularity, nuclear atypia, mitotic activity and microvascular
  proliferation. Mitoses number 6 per 10 high-power fields. On
  immunohistochemistry, the tumour cells are positive for GFAP and OLIG2. The
  Ki-67 proliferation index is approximately 30 per cent. On molecular testing,
  IDH1 R132H is not expressed, there is loss of nuclear H3 K27 trimethylation,
  H3 G34W is not expressed and an H3 K27M mutation is detected.
- Treatment effect: No known presurgical therapy

Integrated diagnosis
- Integrated diagnosis: Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered, CNS WHO grade 4
- Histopathological classification: Not applicable
- CNS WHO grade: 4

Molecular information
- IDH1 R132H (immunohistochemistry): Negative
- H3 trimethylated K27 (immunohistochemistry): Loss of nuclear expression
- H3 G34W (immunohistochemistry): Negative
- H3 mutation (sequencing): H3 K27M detected

Additional findings
- None identified

BRAIN, left thalamus, craniotomy and debulking
- DIFFUSE MIDLINE GLIOMA, H3 K27-altered, CNS WHO grade 4; see synoptic report

MGMT promoter methylation testing has been requested; the result will be issued in a supplementary report.

The case has been referred to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary meeting.
